title: Trump administration disrupts more than $12 billion in education funding; OMB later holds back additional 2026 grants
description_short: Trump administration disrupts more than $12 billion in education funding; OMB later holds back additional 2026 grants
description_medium: Education Week calculated that the Trump administration disrupted at least $12 billion in previously awarded education funding during 2025 through grant cancellations, delayed formula funds, temporary holds, and related actions. In May 2026, Education Week separately reported that OMB was withholding more than $2 billion Congress had appropriated for education programs; legal experts said allowing appropriated funds to expire without congressional approval would amount to unlawful impoundment. The two figures should not be collapsed into a claim that $12 billion was all illegally withheld.
description_long: Education Week calculated that at least $12 billion in previously awarded education funding was disrupted during 2025 through grant cancellations, delayed formula funding, temporary holds and related actions. The supplied correction says that total included more than 730 canceled Education Department grants valued at at least $2.2 billion. Separately, in May 2026, the outlet reported that OMB was withholding more than $2 billion appropriated for over 30 education programs. Legal experts said allowing appropriated funds to expire without congressional approval would constitute unlawful impoundment. The two reports concern different time periods and different collections of actions. A broad estimate of disrupted funding is not identical to an estimate of unlawfully withheld appropriations. Combining them into a claim that the entire $12 billion was illegally withheld would erase that distinction and extend the legal assessment beyond its stated basis. The supported explanation records the scale of disruption and separately attributes the legal concern about the later withholding.

title: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Files Chapter 11 (2004)
description_short: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Files Chapter 11 (2004)
description_medium: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts, Inc. (THCR) and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey on November 21, 2004, in connection with a pre-arranged plan of reorganization, according to the company's SEC Form 10-K for fiscal year 2004. The restructuring support agreement among the debtors, Donald J. Trump, and noteholders was dated October 20, 2004. The company's public indebtedness was approximately $1.8 billion. This was the fourth bankruptcy of a Trump business entity.
description_long: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in New Jersey's federal bankruptcy court on November 21, 2004. The company's SEC Form 10-K describes the filings as part of a prearranged reorganization. A restructuring support agreement among the debtors, Donald Trump and noteholders had been dated October 20, more than a month before the court filing. Keeping those dates separate distinguishes preparation for the restructuring from commencement of the bankruptcy case. The supplied correction places public indebtedness at approximately $1.8 billion, indicating the scale of the obligations involved. The event concerns corporate debtors and their negotiated restructuring, rather than a personal bankruptcy filing by Trump. The earlier drafts also discuss consequences for investors and Trump's continuing position, but the precise financial outcomes should depend on the reorganization terms. The supported account establishes the company, the debt scale and the filing chronology without treating every outstanding obligation as an identical realized loss.
